Encouraging people to draft Coleman in the late rounds was my mission throughout the summer and I reserved room to write about him in each of the first two waiver wire columns this season. 

Stashing Coleman was speculative, since he was technically the Broncos’ No. 3 back behind J.K. Dobbins and RJ Harvey. However, given Dobbins’ injury history (missed time in all six of his NFL campaigns) it seemed almost inevitable that a path would be cleared at some point this season. The coaching staff and beat writers also strongly suggested that Coleman was the direct Dobbins’ replacement, not Harvey. 

Even with all that in mind, I certainly didn’t expect to see Coleman’s opportunity arrive in Week 2. With Harvey sidelined due to a hamstring injury, the rookie had a chance to see the field more on Sunday. Then, Dobbins suffered a hamstring injury of his own, which paved the way for Coleman to help lead the Broncos to victory with 58 scrimmage yards and a score on 13 touches. 

While we wait for updates on both injury statuses, this is your last chance to pick up Coleman… and you’re going to have to spend a significant amount of your budget to do it. Don’t worry, he’ll be worth it. Dobbins hasn’t looked particularly good this season prior to getting hurt and Sean Payton raved about Coleman throughout the preseason. Though Barkley is headed for an early-week MRI, the initial reports seem optimistic that this won’t be a serious issue.

With Price missing time, Wilson leapfrogged George Holani and took over as the early-down back for the Seahawks. The result was a solid 92 yards on 21 carries. 

If Price is unable to suit up for Week 3, Wilson would be a borderline low-end RB2 for fantasy in a matchup where Seattle is 6.5-point favorites over the Commanders. Keep in mind, Zach Charbonnet is expected to return in October, so the runway is short for Wilson.

In Week 2, he picked up where he left off with a 94% route share and an even bigger stat line of 5-95-1 on seven targets.

item.title: How long is Caleb Williams out? Injury update, return date for Bears QB
item.description: Caleb Williams suffered a hamstring injury in the Bears' Week 2 loss to the Vikings. How long will it keep him out? Here is the latest on his status.
item.content:encoded:
The Chicago Bears didn't just lose their Week 2 game to the Minnesota Vikings. They also lost their starting quarterback Caleb Williams to an injury.

Williams suffered a hamstring injury during a first-down scramble in the fourth quarter. The third-year quarterback reached for the back of his leg before sliding to the ground, in pain. He remained down and received medical attention on the field before being carried to the sideline.

Williams was eventually loaded onto a cart and taken to the locker room. He flashed the crowd at Soldier Field a thumbs-up while pumping his fist as he left the field.

Williams was ruled out for the game because of the injury. Now, Bears fans are wondering when exactly he may be able to play again.

Here's what to know about Williams' injury and when he may return to the field.

How long is Caleb Williams out?

It isn't yet clear how much time Williams will miss because of his hamstring injury.

The Bears quarterback is expected to have an MRI to determine the extent of his injury on Monday, per ESPN's Adam Schefter, and that should determine a more concrete timeline for his return.

The Bears are set to play the Philadelphia Eagles on "Monday Night Football" in Week 3.

NANCY ARMOUR: Chicago Bears might have lost more than one game with Caleb Williams injury | Opinion

Caleb Williams injury update

The Bears announced Williams was dealing with a hamstring injury shortly after he exited the game against the Vikings. He was ruled out, but the team did not provide any additional updates on his status after that.

Ben Johnson told reporters following the game Williams was in "good spirits" despite his ailment. The second-year coach said he was not able to estimate the severity of the quarterback's injury but expressed gratitude Williams' knee was not injured.

"I'm actually happy it's nothing with the knee," Johnson said, referencing Williams' injury. "That was my first inclination. But yeah, the hamstring could be pretty damaging as well. So we'll see how bad it is tomorrow and we'll go from there."

Who is Caleb Williams' backup?

Tyson Bagent is the Bears' backup quarterback. The 26-year-old replaced Williams following the 2024 first-round pick's hamstring injury and completed 5 of 9 passes for 54 yards in Chicago's 9-3 loss.

Bagent originally joined the Bears as an undrafted free agent out of Shepherd in 2023. He has started four games in Chicago, and has completed 66.4% of his career passes for 917 yards, three touchdowns and six interceptions.

The Bears think highly of Bagent, as they signed him to a two-year, $10 million extension to be the team's long-term backup quarterback in 2025.

Bears QB depth chart

The Bears currently have three quarterbacks on their 53-man roster, and four within their organization. Here's a look at the pecking order within that unit.

  1. Caleb Williams (injured)
  2. Tyson Bagent
  3. Case Keenum
  4. Miller Moss

As mentioned, Bagent will be elevated into the Bears' starting quarterback role if Williams has to miss time because of his hamstring injury. That would open the door for Keenum to serve as Bagent's backup.

Keenum, 38, has been in the NFL since signing with the Houston Texans as an undrafted free agent in 2012. The Houston product has a 30-36 record and an 84.6 passer rating across 66 career NFL starts. He has played for nine different NFL teams, including the Bears.

Keenum is best-known among NFL fans for his 2017 stint with the Vikings. During that season, he led the team to an 11-3 record across 14 regular-season starts and guided Minnesota to an NFC championship game appearance. He completed 67.6% of his passes for 3,547 yards, 22 touchdowns and seven interceptions while finishing second in the NFL's Comeback Player of the Year award voting.

Finally, Moss is the lone quarterback not on the Bears' 53-man roster. He is currently on the team's practice squad but could be called up to provide additional depth if Williams misses time. The 2026 undrafted free agent played collegiately at USC and Louisville, completing 64.2% of his passes for 2,679 yards, 16 touchdowns and seven interceptions during his lone season with the Cardinals in 2025.

item.title: Vikings are now the betting favorites to win the NFC North
item.description: Heading into the season, the Vikings were a distant fourth in the betting odds to win the NFC North.
item.content:encoded:
Heading into the season, the Vikings were a distant fourth in the betting odds to win the NFC North. A lot can change in two weeks.

The Vikings are now 2-0, with both wins coming against division opponents, a game ahead of the Lions, Packers and Bears, and the new betting favorites to win the division.

The Vikings' odds are +194 to win what looks to be the NFL's most competitive division. The Lions are next at +205, followed by the Packers at +285. Last year's NFC North winners, the Bears, not have the longest odds, at +500, amid concerns that Caleb Williams could miss extended time with a hamstring injury.

Uncertainty at quarterback in Minnesota is an issue, but the Vikings have found a way to win two weeks in a row with Carson Wentz replacing the injured Kyler Murray. The Vikings' defense looks ferocious, and the Vikings look like a playoff team. Something few thought they'd be just a couple weeks ago.

item.title: Rams face Giants as huge questions linger after Australia flop
item.description: The Rams look to bounce back after their putrid opener in Australia but it's unclear how flawed they are heading into game vs. Giants on MNF Sept. 21.
item.content:encoded:
The mystery of the Los Angeles Rams is about to be revealed.

Was the Rams' wacky travel plan largely responsible for their poor play in a 27-7 loss to the San Francisco 49ers in Australia?

Or are the Rams as flawed as they looked in their season opener?

The answer figures to emerge when the Rams (0-1) play the New York Giants (1-0) on Monday Night Football Sept. 21 at SoFi Stadium in Inglewood, Calif.

Los Angeles remains the Super Bowl favorite, and maybe the oddsmakers have taken a cue from Sean McVay, head coach and travel strategist for the Rams.

Of the game in Australia, McVay said, “It's almost like you try to do the 'Men in Black' thing where you say, 'Hey, I don't remember what happened. That was so long ago.'"

But that game deserves analysis in trying to determine if the Rams can bounce back. Here are some things to consider as Los Angeles looks to provide answers to whether it is flawed or was just sleepy vs. the Niners in Week 1.

Good riddance, Australia

McVay never said koalas are evil, or that Crocodile Dundee cannot be trusted or that he'll never eat a shrimp off the barbie. But this week McVay said, “We're not playing in Australia ever again, I hope.’’

Or McVay better hope the Rams arrive in Australia next time far more than 24 hours before kickoff. That and any bad Down Under mojo would be the most palatable explanation for how they played against the 49ers.

49ers are no joke

The Rams did not lose to some Pop Warner team in Australia. In fact, the San Francisco 49ers have emerged as one of the best teams in the league. On Sunday, they scored on their first five possessions and beat the Miami Dolphins 35-13.

In John Harbaugh’s debut as the Giants’ head coach, they beat the Dallas Cowboys 28-20 at home. The victory looks even more impressive after the Cowboys on Sunday beat the Washington Commanders 37-20.

But the talent gap between the 49ers and Giants is substantial.

Paging Matthew Stafford

Vintage Matthew Stafford was AWOL in Australia, and he looked like he should have been napping when he was calling plays.

Or at 38, is Stafford confronting the reality of his age? He turned in a stinker against the 49ers, completing 15-of-25 passes with an interception and failing to throw for a touchdown for the first time in 18 games.

In Stafford's defense, the Rams’ offensive line failed to provide solid protection. He wasn't sacked, but the 49ers registered eight quarterback hits.

Aaron Donald to rescue?

The good news is Los Angeles got an explanation for the shockingly poor debut of Myles Garrett, who was suffering from a knee injury. The bad news is he had arthroscopic surgery and will be out at least until Game 6.

It’s hard to replace a two-time Defensive Player of the Year, but the Rams have one of the best available options – Aaron Donald. Donald, who came out of retirement after two seasons away, is expected on Monday night to make his first start since January 2024. It’d be understandable for him to show some rust. But he’s a three-time NFL Defensive Player of the Year with 111 career sacks and hardly a geriatric at 35.

Ah, a real football stadium

The Rams will be playing at SoFi Stadium, one of the sleekest stadiums in the NFL. L.A. certainly enjoys home cooking and is 32-19 in the regular season and 3-0 in the postseason at the venue.

So could you really expect them to be at their best at Melbourne Cricket Ground?

item.title: Jayden Daniels injury update: Commanders coach Dan Quinn to speak today
item.description: Jayden Daniels, the Commanders' young QB1, dislocated his left elbow during Sunday's loss to the Cowboys. Get the latest updates on his status.
item.content:encoded:
Washington Commanders quarterback Jayden Daniels is dealing with his latest setback from an injury, dislocating his left (non-throwing) elbow in the team's Sunday, Sept. 21, loss to the Dallas Cowboys. It’s the same elbow that cost Daniels, who had perhaps the greatest rookie season in league history in 2024, most of his second professional campaign.

"X-ray showed no fracture,” Commanders head coach Dan Quinn said Sunday evening. “More imaging tomorrow.

"Man, we're bummed for him. I thought he was, like, really playing his (expletive) off. … I was just disheartened for him. Like, I know what he's gone through.”

Quinn is scheduled to provide an update on Daniels’ injury and prognosis Monday afternoon.

What is Jayden Daniels' injury history in the NFL?

Unfortunately for the Commanders, Daniels has been no stranger to injury in his short NFL career, that despite playing all 17 games and the playoffs as a rookie in 2024.

▶ 2025: Missed Weeks 3-4 (knee)

▶ 2025: Missed Week 8 (hamstring)

▶ 2025: Missed Weeks 10-13 (left elbow)

▶ 2025: Missed Weeks 15-18 (left elbow)

Reaction to Jayden Daniels' injury

Even when Daniels, the second overall pick of the 2024 NFL Draft, was coming out of college − at Arizona State and LSU, where he won the Heisman Trophy − there were concerns about how he'd hold up physically in the NFL given his slender frame and tendency to leave the pocket.

"I think some of it is bad luck. But we know Jayden Daniels, he's a slimmer-bodied individual, alright? He's also a quarterback that will take off. He's also a quarterback that he's an ultimate competitor," NFL Network analyst Michael Robinson, a Pro Bowl fullback during his playing days, said Sunday night.

"If I'm Jayden, I would really look at in the offseason putting on a just a little bit of weight. This is still tackle football, this is still a physical game."

item.content:encoded:
The Minnesota Vikings visited the Chicago Bears and the result was the same as it has been for quite a while now: a Vikings victory. Minnesota has now won seven consecutive games at Soldier Field, a stadium that used to be a house of horrors for Vikings fans.

The offense never really found its rhythm, but the defense more than made up for it. Brian Flores’ unit was all over Caleb Williams and Tyson Bagent from start to finish. The pass rush consistently disrupted the pocket, the secondary kept everything in front of them, and the Bears struggled to generate any explosive plays. It wasn’t flashy; more like an old school NFC Central matchup.

The Vikings played great defense, won the field position battle, controlled the line of scrimmage, and found a way to leave Chicago with another win and that’s all that matters.

Dallas Turner

Turner finished with four quarterback hits and two sacks, and those numbers hardly tell the whole story. He lived in the Bears’ backfield all afternoon, and if not for Caleb Williams’ ability to escape pressure, Turner might have added two or three more sacks to his total.

This is exactly what the Vikings envisioned when they selected him in the first round. His game-clinching sack of Tyson Bagent was the perfect ending to another dominant performance.

Jalen Redmond

Redmond’s third-quarter play may have been the biggest moment of the game.

His forced fumble on D’Andre Swift completely changed the momentum and prevented what looked like a potential scoring drive. Redmond continues to be a disruptive force in the middle of the defense, creating opportunities for others while making plenty of plays himself.

His impact doesn’t always show up on the stat sheet, but it was impossible to miss in this game.

Isaiah Rodgers

Rodgers delivered two of the biggest plays of the afternoon.

His blocked field goal in the fourth quarter helped preserve the Vikings’ lead at a critical moment. Earlier, he recovered the fumble forced by Redmond near the goal line, preventing the Bears from capitalizing on a scoring opportunity.

He also turned in another strong performance in coverage against an offense that had put up impressive numbers the previous week.

Brian Flores

I had high expectations for this defense entering the season.

I had no idea it could be this good.

Flores has built one of the most disruptive defenses in football. The pass rush comes from everywhere, the secondary is disciplined, and opposing quarterbacks rarely look comfortable. The unit has been so dominant that there are times I feel more confident when the defense takes the field than when the offense does. The Vikings’ defense has become the identity of this team, and Flores deserves enormous credit for what he has built. It’s hard to imagine anyone doing a better job than he has this season.

item.title: Eagles News: “Sean Mannion took a big step forward this week”
item.description: Philadelphia Eagles news and links for 9/21/26.
item.content:encoded:
Welcome to The Linc, the daily Philadelphia Eagles links roundup at Bleeding Green Nation!

Music City Magic – Iggles Blitz

I thought Sean Mannion took a big step forward this week. The Eagles gained 341 yards and had 23 first downs (only had 10 last week). There are still things to work on, like getting rid of the passes to Makai Lemon behind the line of scrimmage. But overall Mannion did a good job. The run game was more creative. We saw Hollywood Brown on a couple of end around plays. And Mannion made a nice adjustment on the winning TD.

Judging the biggest overreactions to NFL Week 2 games – ESPN

Sure, Hurts was pressured a lot, but he was awesome Sunday when pressured. He was 11-for-20 for 137 yards and two touchdowns, including the winning TD in the final seconds. Saquon Barkley left this game early with an injury, and although he came back briefly in the second half, he wasn’t able to finish the contest. That surely emboldened the Titans’ pressure plan. I get that it doesn’t look great or smooth. But it’s Week 2, and the Eagles are 2-0 while they’re putting things together. Two of the big questions coming into this season were whether Hurts could thrive with all the change that was made around him and whether DeVonta Smith could fill the No. 1 receiver role with A.J. Brown traded to New England. Well, Hurts was heroic in leading the comeback, and Smith caught 10 passes for 117 yards and a touchdown. There are a lot of offenses with a lot less hope than the Eagles deserve to have in theirs right now.

Eagles vs. Titans: 7 winners, 5 losers, 5 IDKs – BGN

If you didn’t watch the game and only looked at the box score, you might think Hurts had a relatively pedestrian day at the office: 26/37 (70.3 completion), 264 yards (7.1 average), 2 TD, 2 INT, 85.9 passer rating … 5 carries, 16 rushing yards. But such a sentiment couldn’t be further from the case. Hurts was a huge reason why the Eagles won this game. Let’s start at the end. The Eagles were down three points at their own 35-yard line with 1:56 on the clock and zero timeouts to work with. Hurts led a nine-play, 65-yard drive where he accounted for all of those yards (61 passing, four rushing) and the game-winning touchdown pass. His only two incompletions were a short drop by Dontayvion Wicks and a throwaway to avoid a sack with pressure quickly reaching him. Hurts delivered in the clutch. It was a well-deserved ending for him, too, since he was tasked with carrying the offense for most of the game. The Eagles did Hurts no favors by insisting on sticking with an ineffective running game on early downs … which forced the offense into way too many third-and-longs. Hurts made some really good throws in those situations to sustain drives.

Eagles 24 Titans 20 quick recap – Music City Miracles

There are no moral victories in the NFL, but the Tennessee Titans, as a team, have a lot to be proud of even in the 24-20 loss to the Philadelphia Eagles. After the way they played last week, I was 100% sure they were going to lose by 3 touchdowns. They fought all the way to the finish today. There is still a lot of stuff to clean up. The defense was on the field the entire first half. They have to find a way to get off the field. To their credit, they were much better in the second half. They also picked Jalen Hurts off twice in the loss. They still need more from the offense. Part of the reason the defense was on the field so much in the first half was because the offense couldn’t sustain a drive.

Eagles-Titans Postgame: Eagles 2-0, Jalen Hurts Delivers Game-Winning TD To Darius Cooper – PHLY Eagles

Super Bowl champion Vinny Curry is with us to break down Jalen Hurts’ game-winning drive that delivered the Eagles a 24-20 win and included two spectacular DeVonta Smith catches. We break down a wild game that included two interceptions by Jalen Hurts, injuries to Saquon Barkley and Dallas Goedert, and some weird football. No matter, the Eagles escaped to stay undefeated. Miles Johnston, Brandon Lee Gowton and Bo Wulf join Curry, with insight from EJ Smith from the Eagles locker room and Fran Duffy on the plays you need to know.

Eagles and Titans players had their cleats melting in 157-degree heat – SB Nation

Not only did players see their cleats physically melting on the field, but the heat caused the composition of the cleats to change, with Jordan Mailata saying that he rolled his ankle twice on Sunday — and believed it could have been caused by the plastic of his cleats becoming soft due to the heat. Conditions were so extreme that Eagles head coach Nick Sirianni got an IV at halftime to prevent dehydration, which came from just standing on the surface for 90 minutes. Players struggled to keep cool, and it’s raising more questions about player safety due to weather-related events, especially as it pertains to playing surfaces.

Given the chance to mask Eagles’ offensive woes, Jalen Hurts ‘didn’t flinch’ in clutch time vs. the Titans – PHLY Eagles

He found Dontayvion Wicks for a 20-yard completion with the Eagles facing third-and-6 near midfield and hit DeVonta Smith, who pulled off two acrobatic catches on the final drive, for a 19 yard completion facing the same down and distance a few plays later. And with the Eagles facing first-and-goal from the three-yard line, Hurts rolled to his right and found Darius Cooper wide open in the middle of the end zone to secure the decisive lead. “That motherfucker balled out today,” Eagles left tackle Jordan Mailata said. “Jalen really got in his bag today and just started dialing everything up and hitting everyone.”

Handing out 10 awards from the Eagles-Titans game – PhillyVoice

4) The ‘Dirty Work’ Award 🧹🧽: Darius Cooper. Being the dirty work receiver is hard. You play special teams and when you get in the game on offense you’re usually just blocking or running pick plays for the star players. And yet, when you get your opportunities, you sure as hell better be ready because you’re not going to get many of them. Cooper had two catches for 26 yards, and the game-winning TD.

2026 NFL season, Week 2: What We Learned from Sunday’s games – NFL.com

Hurts comes in clutch after tough outing. It wasn’t the best day at the office for Jalen Hurts, but when met with a deadline — needing to lead a game-winning drive with 1:56 remaining — the Super Bowl LIX Most Valuable Player delivered. Hurts, who threw a bad interception in the end zone during his first possession and another pick during the drive immediately preceding his last, led Philly on a nine-play, 65-yard drive to take the lead and the win from the Titans. He did so by becoming laser-focused on DeVonta Smith, throwing to the Eagles’ No. 1 wide receiver on four of eight passes, including a pretty 19-yard gain on third-and-6 to set up Philadelphia at the goal line. On the next play, he hit Darius Cooper for the wideout’s first career touchdown to propel the Eagles to a surprisingly difficult win. He wasn’t nearly perfect Sunday, going 26 of 37 for 264 yards, two touchdowns and the two picks, but he was clutch as ever when called upon to leave Titans fans with some achy, breaky hearts.

The Eagles need Jalen Hurts 2.0 now more than ever. His evolution and clutch gene are carrying a rough offense. – Inquirer

But there was something unique about Hurts carrying the offense at the scorching Nissan Stadium on Sunday. He’s strapped the Eagles on his back before. He’s had better games against better opponents when the stakes were much higher. He’s been clutch on many previous occasions. No, this was a different Hurts. This was the 2.0 version. This was Hurts evolving as a quarterback in a new scheme that gives him more freedom as a passer. We saw glimpses of it in Week 1 vs. the Commanders. He took another step in Week 2. If the narrative entering this season was that the 28-year-old faced a make-it-or-break-it tipping point, after another offensive coordinator change and a seemingly unresolved contract situation, Hurts has shown through two weeks that he’s making it.

Eagles escape Titans with an ‘organizational win.’ Can continuity help the O-line? – The Athletic

Hurts believes “building in-game chemistry” can lead to progress, especially on the offensive line. He intimated his desire for continuity by stressing on Wednesday that he’d “been working with Cam” at center — not Kendall. The drastic nature of the Eagles’ position moves after placing Landon Dickerson on injured reserve should not go unnoticed. Jurgens said he had never taken reps at left guard until last week’s practices. Sirianni said the Eagles chose to move Jurgens, a two-time Pro Bowler at center, and play Kendall at center because it was Kendall’s “most natural” position. By prioritizing Kendall, the Eagles aimed to create continuity instead of possibly cycling options at left guard next to Jurgens. It also creates a longer runway for cohesion while Dickerson misses at least four games — or more. “Now we have our starting five moving on,” left tackle Jordan Mailata said. “Now we have film on how we’re getting beat, how we’re not getting beat, and things to work on.” Philadelphia’s shaky play on the offensive line reflected the suddenness of the changes. Jurgens said the coaching staff informed him of the change “early in the week.” He’d played right guard in 2022 and 2023 — but in a vertical blocking system under former offensive line coach Jeff Stoutland. Jurgens said he was “excited,” “nervous,” and “anxious” about debuting at left guard, with techniques in which he said, “everything’s different.”

Roob’s Observations after Hurts leads magical game-winning drive over Titans – NBCSP

Dallas Goedert’s knee injury really puts the spotlight on just how badly the Eagles need to beef up the tight end room. Johnny Mundt is a good blocker but he’s not a pass catcher and E.J. Jenkins has one career reception, and when Goedert is out they really don’t have a second receiving option at tight end. The Eagles drafted Eli Stowers in the second round, but after a lackluster training camp he went on Injured Reserve and who knows when he’ll be back. We’ve been talking about this all summer. The room is just not good enough and while we don’t know how serious Goedert’s injury is yet, either way Howie Roseman needs to find a second tight end who can catch the football. Zach Ertz makes the most sense, but it has to be someone. Their tight end stable right now is just not good enough.

Bears vs. Eagles odds: Opening lines for Week 3 matchup – Windy City Gridiron

Our friends at FanDuel Sportsbook currently have the line for next Monday night’s game at Bears +3.5. Chicago being an underdog at home, even against a very good Eagles team, has to be because Caleb is expected to be out. That makes me wonder how much of a swing the oddsmakers put on Chicago’s QB1. When top-tier quarterbacks around the league are out, the line is often moved by a touchdown, so is that what’s happening here?

Initial hope is that Caleb Williams has a Grade 1 hamstring strain – PFT

The hope, we’re told, is that it will be diagnosed as a Grade 1 injury. That’s the lowest level, with minimal tearing of the muscle fibers. Ultimately, the MRI will show the extent of the injury. And even if it’s only a Grade 1 strain, it’s possible he won’t be ready to go in eight days, when the Bears host the Eagles on Monday Night Football. If Williams can’t go, it will be Tyson Bagent. Who performed well in limited duty on Sunday, and in whom the Bears have a high degree of confidence.

Albert Breer’s Takeaways: How the Browns Have Weathered the Deshaun Watson Storm—for Now – SI

And, yes, Caleb Williams got hurt (more on that in a minute). Still, he was hardly himself before that—throwing for 138 yards and an interception on 15-of-26 passing—and Chicago couldn’t crack 300 yards after exceeding 250 both on the ground and through the air in Carolina in Week 1. Along the way, the Vikings got a fourth-down goal-line stop in the third quarter and two more red-zone stops on Chicago’s last two offensive possessions, one led by Williams and the other by backup Tyson Bagent (a Dallas Turner sack ended that one).

Former NY Giants GM Ernie Accorsi passes away – Big Blue View

The New York Giants announced Sunday afternoon that former general manager Ernie Accorsi passed away on Saturday night at the age of 84. Accorsi was born on October 29th, 1941 in Hershey Pennsylvania and spent 37 years as an NFL executive, the final 12 of which were spent with the Giants. He first joined the Giants’ front office as an assistant under George Young, serving in that capacity for four years. Accorsi became the Giants’ GM in 1998 and ran the Giants’ front office until 2026. Accorsi built the Giants’ 2000 NFC Championship team, and along with Jerry Reese and Dave Gettleman, laid the foundation for the Giants’ 2007 Super Bowl Championship.

10 thoughts on the Cowboys 37-20 win over the Commanders – Blogging The Boys

Same ol’ issues The win is nice, but the defense did not look good. They got pressure at times, but never got home. No sacks. They also had problems in coverage with wide-open receivers finding creases similar to last week. Despite losing by 17, the Commanders still ran more plays, gained more yards, and had the ball longer. This Cowboys’ defense still has issues. Was it an improvement over last week? Yes, but not by a lot, and one can’t wonder that had Daniels not gotten hurt, the Cowboys could be looking at an 0-2 start.

Commanders QB Jayden Daniels injured vs. Dallas Cowboys – Hogs Haven

Commanders quarterback Jayden Daniels suffered what looked to be a significant injury at the end of the first half of Sunday’s game against the Dallas Cowboys. He was carted off the field in clear pain with a left elbow injury. The Commanders ruled him out with an elbow injury shortly after. Backup Marcus Mariota took over in the second half. After the 37-20 loss to Dallas, Commanders head coach Dan Quinn confirmed the elbow dislocation but said there was no fracture. Daniels is set to fly home from Dallas with the Commanders. He’ll have more imaging done on the elbow on Monday. Daniels also dislocated his left elbow last season, which eventually cut his 2025 campaign short.

item.title: Bengals News: 2-0 and it feels so good
item.description: The defense once again stamps its identity on the win.
item.content:encoded:
Wow what a difference a year makes. The Cincinnati Bengals are once again 2-0, and this time there is actual optimism to go along with that. It also hasn’t been Joe Burrow, Ja’Marr Chase and Tee Higgins carrying the team on their back to the wins. In fact, quite the contrary. The defense has been holding up the offense, and that has not gone without notice from the quarterback.

“It feels like early on in 2021,” Burrow told Geoff Hobson from Bengals.com. “We’ve got a really good defense, and try to stay in front of the sticks, not turn the ball over, kick field goals, put points on the board, we’re going to win with our defense.”

Back in 2021 you had players like linebackers Germaine Pratt and Logan Wilson as well as several secondary guys like Jessie Bates, Chidobe Awuzie and Mike Hilton who could make the defensive plays at the end of the games to seal things out. That is something this team hasn’t really had these past few seasons. It takes so much pressure off an offense when you don’t have to assume the other team is going to score nearly every time.

Some fans may get riled up by this, but truly this offense has not bloomed yet. It mostly looked to not make the big mistake against Houston. The Cleveland Browns certainly got their first win pretty early this season. They also looked generally good on the day, but we will have to see how long that continues. To have this kind of rant after their recent history with Deshaun Watson at quarterback is kind of comical.

Jim Harbaugh ‘not deterred’ by Chargers’ 0-2 start following double-digit loss to Raiders

Things are not great for the Los Angeles Chargers. A vast majority of people would have expected them to start 2-0, but instead they sit at 0-2 with a huge hole to dig out of. So much for that Justin Herbert finally having that year their fans have dreamed about.

2026 NFL season, Week 2: What We Learned from Sunday’s games

The Bengals did not allow a single touchdown in Week 2 at the Texans, their first game allowing no touchdowns since Week 3, 2022, at the Jets. item.title: Fox audio issues had some viewers watching one game, hearing Vikings-Bears
item.description: The second Sunday of the 2026 regular season gave new meaning to the second-game experience.
item.content:encoded:
The second Sunday of the 2026 regular season gave new meaning to the second-game experience.

As noted by Megan Armstrong of Awful Announcing, multiple viewers of the Packers-Jets and Falcons-Panthers games on Fox complained that the sound was replaced with audio from Bears-Vikings.

Armstrong's story includes multiple tweets, including visual/audio evidence.

A PFT reader emailed the same concern.

"My husband and I were watching the Packers/Jets game on FOX today," the reader said. "Twice, we lost the audio for our game and were listening to the Vikings/Bears game. The first time only lasted about a minute but the second time was at least 5-6 minutes. So we're watching the Pack and listening to the Vikes."

In nearly 25 years of doing this, audio from one game making its way into another game is a first. And hopefully it's the last time something like that will happen.

item.title: Chargers star safety provides his own injury update before Week 3’s game vs. Bills
item.description: How limited will James be in Week 3 against Bills?
item.content:encoded:
The Los Angeles Chargers have started 0-2 after consecutive 26-14 losses to the Arizona Cardinals and Las Vegas Raiders, and in Week 2, their superstar safety Derwin James injured his hand.

The six-time All-Pro updated his injury on Monday as the club begins preparations for the cross-country trip to take on the Buffalo Bills in Week 3.

Despite fracturing the pinky against the Raiders, James still appeared on 52 defensive snaps, the second-most of any Chargers player on that side of the ball. He’s always been one of the tougher defensive backs in football.

He’s regularly been darn disruptive too.

Now 30, James was a second-team All-Pro the past two seasons.

Through two contests this year, James has 17 tackles and one pass breakup.

At 6’2” and 215 pounds, the former All-American from Florida State remains one of the NFL’s most dangerous swiss-army knives in the secondary. He’s an elite blitzer, tackler, and coverage defender.

It’ll be interesting to see how sizable his cast is, and monitor whether it hinders his ability to make plays on the football against the Bills in Week 3 (and for the remainder of the season).

item.title: Stock Up, Stock Down After the Broncos’ Week 2 Comeback Win Over the Jaguars
item.description: Stock up and stock down is a weekly series where I go through the Denver Broncos roster and give you stock-ups and stock-downs on every player currently on the 53-man roster. item.content:encoded:
Stock Up, Stock Down After the Broncos’ Week 2 Comeback Win Over the Jaguars

What a difference a week makes.

The Denver Broncos were coming off an embarrassing blowout loss to the Kansas City Chiefs on Monday Night Football, and things looked dire in Broncos Country. The offense looked bad, Bo Nix had one of his worst career games, Davis Webb’s debut as a playcaller was a failure, and the defense looked bad and had a ton of missed tackles.

To make things worse, the Broncos would be hosting their home opener vs. a very good Jacksonville Jaguars team that has been playing like one of the better teams in the league and beat the Broncos by double digits last season.

Well, the Broncos bounced back and had one of their classic 4th-quarter comeback victories. Things started rough early on, but the defense played well, and Bo Nix, Jaylen Waddle, and rookie Jonah Coleman helped lead the Broncos to a victory.

Stock up and stock down is a weekly series where I go through the Denver Broncos roster and give you stock-ups and stock-downs on every player currently on the 53-man roster. After a bounce-back performance like that on Sunday, we are going to see a lot more stock-ups than we did last week.

Quarterback

Bo Nix – Stock up: After having one of the worst games of his career on Monday Night, Nix bounced back and gave us a classic Bo Nix performance. There were some struggles early on, but he was moving the ball up and down the field fairly easily against the Jaguars’ defense. However, red zone struggles really hurt what could have been a big game for Nix. Still, he passed for 288 yards and a touchdown and led yet another 4th-quarter comeback vs. a pretty good Jaguars team.

Jarrett Stidham – Unchanged: Remains the backup quarterback

Sam Ehlinger – Unchanged: Remains the emergency third-string quarterback

Running Back

JK Dobbins – Stock down: The veteran back left the game due to a hamstring injury, which thankfully sounds minor, but we’ll see how it trends as the week progresses. With his injury history, it is concerning to see an injury pop up this early in the season. Pair that with his multiple goal-line failures and rookie Jonah Coleman looking really good, and you have to go stock down on JK Dobbins.

RJ Harvey – Unchanged: Harvey was inactive for this game due to a hamstring injury, but he was able to put in two limited practices, so it sounds like he may not miss much more time moving forward. I am going with unchanged simply because his role is not in danger. He is the Broncos third down/pass game specialist. We saw him get plenty of touches and snaps in the opener, and when healthy, I believe his role is locked in on this offense.

Jonah Coleman – Stock up: Coleman entered the game late due to JK Dobbins leaving with a hamstring injury and played really well. He scored his first career touchdown, which was the go-ahead score, and helped the Broncos ice the game late, which has been something they have struggled to do in recent history. Coleman is the future starter of this backfield; it’s just a matter of when, not if.

Tyler Badie – Stock up: I thought Badie played well. He had a 27-yard catch-and-run and had a couple of nice returns in the kicking game. That’s what he’s supposed to do, and I thought he played well, all things considered.

Adam Prentice – Stock down: He played just 8 snaps of offense and wasn’t used in the Broncos’ goal-line failures in the first half. He was a short-yardage specialist last season and in the preseason, but the Broncos have yet to pull that trigger this season.

Wide Receiver

Jaylen Waddle – Stock way up: That’s more like it. After a 1-catch for 2-yard performance in Week 1, Waddle exploded for 8 catches for 138 yards. He made multiple key plays in big moments and looked like the explosive playmaker the Broncos traded for this offseason. This should be the first of many big games from the Broncos’ explosive wide receiver.

Courtland Sutton – Stock down: His role in this offense appears to have taken a step back. Had a down Week 1, and unlike Waddle, the veteran didn’t do too much in Week 2. He finished with 3 catches for 25 yards and was targeted just 4 times. I still feel like we’ll have a few big Sutton games, but his week-to-week performance is probably going to continue to be inconsistent.

Pat Bryant – Unchanged: 0 targets and 1 end-around for 16 yards. It wasn’t a great game on paper for Bryant, who was also flagged for another holding call (Like the other ones on Monday Night; it seemed kinda BS), but I am not going to overreact here. The team really likes their second-year wide receiver, and this week was just the Jaylen Waddle show.

Marvin Mims Jr. – Stock down: Injuries suck. The Broncos All-Pro returner has been dealing with multiple injuries throughout the summer. He missed time during camp, returned for the preseason, and then was hurt again; he played in Week 1, got hurt, and then missed Week 2. He just needs to get healthy and stay healthy.

Troy Franklin – Stock up: I went with stock down due to his bad OPI on Monday Night, but I am going with stock up due to his nice one-handed catch on Sunday. He played just 13 snaps and was targeted 2 times, so the usage isn’t great, but he made the most of his opportunity on Sunday.

Lil’Jordan Humphrey – Unchanged: He is who he is and fills a depth role on the offense and special teams. He didn’t play much on Sunday, but that was expected.

Tight End

Adam Trautman – Unchanged: An in-line blocking specialist who played 65% of the snaps, but you wouldn’t really know it if you watched the game. 0 targets and was strictly in for blocking.

Evan Engram – Stock up: He was targeted just once on Sunday but made a tremendous catch late in the game. He played 52% of the snaps and made the most of his lone target, so I am going stock up.

Nate Adkins – Stock up: Is Nate Adkins really the Joker? (Sorry). The blocking specialist led all tight ends with 3 catches for 32 yards and 1 touchdown. He actually had the second-most receiving yards on the team, only trailing Jaylen Waddle. He played 37% of the offensive snaps, contributed on special teams, and does all the dirty work that typically goes unrecognized by fans. Need games like this from your depth players throughout the year.

Dallen Bentley – Unchanged: The rookie tight end was inactive and is likely having a red-shirt year for the Broncos.

Offensive Line

Garett Bolles – Unchanged: I’ll say this each week, I am not an OL expert, but the unit looked better this week. Nix was not sacked, and I did not see the pressure get to him as it did vs. the Chiefs.

Ben Powers – Unchanged: Same story here with Powers. Did not really notice him, which is usually a good thing for a lineman.

Luke Wattenberg – Stock down: Simply for the delayed snap on the 3rd-down goal-line toss play. It threw off the play from the start, which immediately doomed it from the start.

Quinn Meinerz: Stock up: He pancaked a dude.

Mike McGlinchey – Stock up: Struggled vs. the Chiefs but appeared to have a better game on Sunday.

Alex Palczewski – Unchanged: Played just 4 offensive snaps and is your top reserve OL.

Matt Peart – Unchanged: Didn’t play a single snap but is your backup tackle.

Alex Forsyth – Unchanged: Did not play a single snap but is your backup center.

Kage Casey – Unchanged: Inactive and likely having a rookie redshirt year.

Defensive Line

Zach Allen – Stock up: He’s unblockable at times and was in there on multiple pressures and sacks despite not being credited with one.

DJ Jones – Stock up: The run defense was better, and he’s the man in the middle of the defensive line. I did not see him stand out much, but the overall play was better than last week, so stock up.

Malcolm Roach – Stock up: Roach had a sack, and the unit played better in Week 2.

Eyioma Uwazurike – Stock up: Enyi got the start on Sunday, if you care about that, and played in 46% of the defensive snaps vs. the Jaguars. He’s a key starter/rotational player for the Broncos’ defensive line.

Sai’vion Jones – Stock up: He was active over rookie Tyler Onyedim and played 10% of the snaps on Sunday. I am going with stock up due to him helping to force a TFL late. This is the first time I noticed him make an impact play, so we are going with stock up.

Tyler Onyedim – Unchanged: Inactive and likely having a rookie redshirt year.

Jordan Jackson – Unchanged: Inactive depth player.

Edge Rushers

Nik Bonitto – Stock slightly down: Bonitto had a strip sack called back early in the game due to an iffy defensive holding call on Riley Moss, but outside of that, his impact wasn’t what I expected. We’re through 2 games, and he has 0 sacks. He has been applying pressure, but he’s paid to get those sacks and is viewed as a 12+ sack guy. So, I am going slightly down, but simply because I want to see him get after the quarterback more.

Jonah Elliss – Stock up: He played better in Week 2 and played 69% of the defensive snaps. Elliss got after Jags QB Trevor Lawrence on a third down, forced an incompletion, and applied pressure throughout. It wasn’t a great game, but an improvement from what we saw on Monday Night.

Que Robinson – Stock up: I think he’s the future starter at edge rusher and picked up another sack on Sunday. He has the size, speed, athleticism, and talent to be a disruptive pass rusher off the edge, and we’re seeing that early on this season. I think he’ll surpass Elliss as the season moves on.

Dondrea Tillman – Unchanged: Played 31% of the snaps and is a rotational edge for the Broncos. He’s behind Jonah and Que, but does provide some much-needed depth at the position.

Linebackers

Alex Singleton – Stock up: Singleton is who he is and has been during his entire time with the Broncos. However, he and the entire defense played better on Sunday, so stock up.

Justin Strnad – Stock up: I didn’t notice him a ton on Sunday, but the unit played better, and the defense held the Jags under 100 yards rushing, and their tight ends didn’t make many plays, so stock up for Strnad.

Jordan Turner – Unchanged: 0 snaps on defense but played 83% of the special teams snaps.

Karene Reid – Unchanged: 0 snaps on defense but played 52% of the snaps on special teams.

Cornerback

Pat Surtain II – Stock up: He’s CB1 and locked down Brian Thomas Jr. for most of the game.

Riley Moss – Stock up: Moss had a great game and had a game-changing, momentum-flipping INT. It was a really good game by the Broncos’ corner.

Ja’Quan McMillian – Unchanged: Parker Washington made some plays on Sunday, but J-Mac came up big late and had a near INT in the 4th quarter. I am going with unchanged simply due to Washington popping off again.

Jahdae Barron – Stock down: Barron played just 2 defensive snaps on Sunday and 43% of the special teams snaps. He didn’t play much in Week 1, but I chalked it up to game script and a run-heavy Chiefs team. Can’t do that this week, so this will be something to watch moving forward.

Kris Abrams-Draine – Unchanged: He’s the 5th cornerback and played 0 defensive snaps but 57% of the special teams plays. He also makes me nervous when he’s out returning punts.

Safety

Talanoa Hufanga – Unchanged: He was out there, but I did not see him make many big impact plays. The defense played well as a unit, so that’s encouraging, but I didn’t see anything too noteworthy from Hufanga. He did have that dumb delay-of-game penalty before halftime, but that probably didn’t impact the outcome of that drive much.

Brandon Jones – Unchanged: I thought he made a few nice open-field tackles on Sunday, but like Hufanga, the Broncos safety had nothing super noteworthy overall.

Devon Key – Unchanged: Played 83% of the Broncos special teams snaps.

JL Skinner –Unchanged: Skinner saw 1 defensive snap on Sunday and played 65% of the special teams snaps.

Tycen Anderson – Unchanged: Played 65% of the Broncos special teams snaps.

Special Teams

Wil Lutz – Unchanged: 2/2 on kicks and 2/2 on XPs

Jeremy Crawshaw – Unchanged: Had 3 punts and averaged 45 yards per boot, but didn’t pin the Jags inside the 20 on Sunday.

Mitchell Fraboni – Unchanged: Played 7 snaps and snapped the ball well on all 7.

item.title: Shane Steichen on 9 straight losses: We're right there, have to find a way to win at the end
item.description: After the conclusion of the 2025 season in January, Colts owner Carlie Irsay-Gordon made it clear that General Manager Chris Ballard and head coach Shane Steichen had to put a better product on the field in 2026.
item.content:encoded:
After the conclusion of the 2025 season in January, Colts owner Carlie Irsay-Gordon made it clear that General Manager Chris Ballard and head coach Shane Steichen had to put a better product on the field in 2026.

“We have been very clear with Chris and Shane that giving them another opportunity means that the sense of urgency for them to deliver and perform has never been higher,” Irsay-Gordon said at her press conference after announcing that Ballard and Steichen would both return.

But with Sunday’s overtime loss to Kansas City, Indianapolis has now lost nine consecutive games dating back to Week 12 of last season. The team finished 8-9 after starting 8-2 and has now dropped the first two this season.

A lot has happened along the way — including starting quarterback Daniel Jones going down with a torn Achilles. But in a results-oriented business, Indianapolis has not been good enough.

At the end of his postgame press conference on Sunday night, Steichen was asked what he tells the team after nine consecutive losses.

“I tell them to keep your freaking heads up, dude,” Steichen said. “It is a long season ahead of us. We are battling like crazy. That’s the message. We have to continue to grow and learn. There is a lot of football left. Like I said last week, we are right there. We have to find a way to win at the end. That was one of those games.

“It is a freaking hard-ass league, and you have got to find a way to win these tight games.”

The Colts will be back at home next weekend to face a division rival, the 0-2 Texans.

item.title: Commanders vs. Cowboys (game one) – Studs and Duds
item.description: Stefon Diggs, Amik Robertson saw stock go up, Daron Payne, Mike Sainristil saw stock go down after Commanders loss
item.content:encoded:
Heartbreak is not a foreign word to Commanders fans. The team has gone through so much in the last two decades that most newer fans take this to be the norm.

Well, heartbreak hit again, this time at the hands of one of Washington’s fiercest rivals — the Dallas Cowboys. Washington couldn’t stop a toddler’s nosebleed, however quarterback Jayden Daniels was keeping the team within striking distance and it looked like Washington may pull out a score before the half, while getting the ball to open the second half of play.

Then disaster hit…

As if the injury to Jayden Daniels wasn’t enough, Washington, behind veteran backup quarterback Marcus Mariota, had to battle the refs and a costly fumble in Dallas territory. The circumstances were too much to overcome as the Commanders fell 37-20 to their most bitter rival on the road.

Washington is now 0-2 on the young season as they get set to face the defending Super Bowl champion Seahawks at home next Sunday at 1 p.m. ET.

Below are my Studs and Duds of the game, followed by some notes.

Studs:

  • QB Jayden Daniels: I feel so bad for the young man. He was having a great first half before the Gaffe-at-the-Goal-line occurred. He did miss a WIDE OPEN Treylon Burks, who had five yards of separation on a deep ball, but otherwise he was wheeling and dealing. The Cowboys had no answer for his scrambling in the first half, as he put up 69 yards on seven improvised runs.
  • WR Stefon Diggs: Diggs had five catches for 47 yards and two touchdowns. He has three scores on the young season already after recording four TDs last year with New England.
  • CB Amik Robertson: On what was an ugly day for the Commanders secondary, Mik continues to be one of the bright spots. He was targeted seven times and gave up just four receptions for 37 yards while recording two passes defended. He had five tackles, all solo.
  • QB Marcus Mariota: Given the circumstances, I thought Mariota played very well. He had the touchdown to Diggs and absolutely should have had another on a beautiful pass to Dyami Brown which the officials stole. Overall, in a half of play, he was 11-for-16 for 111 yards and a touchdown while taking zero sacks. He looked in control of Blough’s offense.

Duds:

  • Daron Haynesworth: I’m done defending him. I HATED when we took him over Derwin James and I’ll NEVER let that go! At this point, he’s just stealing money from owner Josh Harris. I GUARANTEE Ricky Barber would have at least given some effort.
  • CB Mike StandRealStill: Another week, another chance for opposing quarterbacks to pick on StandRealStill. Yet again, he was the worst of the Commanders corners, allowing five receptions on six targets for 73 yards and was responsible for one touchdown. He needs to be benched! Period!
  • S Jeremy Reaves: Reaves just isn’t cutting it as a free safety. I’d much rather Quan Martin get reps as the free safety with Tyler Owens getting time as the third safety. Reavo may stuff the stat sheet with a good number of tackles, but he looks absolutely lost in coverage.
  • LB Leo Chenal: Fans were hyped when Washington signed Chenal to a free agent contract. I fell into that hype a bit, too. But, before free agency hit, I was not on board with us targeting him because I said he struggled a LOT in coverage (see Tweet below). Well, over two games, those struggles have reared their ugly head. Not only has Chenal been poor in coverage, but he’s missed quite a few tackles. Despite leading the team with 12 combined tackles (six solo), he looked absolutely HORRIBLE in coverage.
  • HC Dan Quinn: Talk about being on the Hot Seat! Dan Quinn’s backside might be so hot right now, that if he tried to wipe with extra-soft Charmin, he’d likely go up in flames! But Mark, that’s not very professional of you… You know what — we’re past that point! He’s officially a lame duck!
  • Shawn Hochuli and his crew: The officiating during this game was absolutely terrible. The non-touchdown to Dyami Brown was a suspendable-without-pay offense. This “crew” needs to be investigated by the NFL.

Notes:

  • RB Rachaad White led all Commanders with six receptions, which he turned into 40 receiving yards. He ran the ball well between the tackles, picking up 43 yards on just seven carries. I debated giving him Stud status.
  • DL Javon Kinlaw recorded his first sack with the Commanders. He also had a tackle for a loss and two pressures on the afternoon.
  • EDGE K’Lavon Chaisson notched his first sack with the Commanders on a great effort play off the left edge on a third down inside the red zone, forcing Dallas to kick the field goal. He had three total tackles and two pressures to go along with his sack.
  • LG Chris Paul is too unathletic to be used in space. He’s a phone-booth player and that’s about it. This is the second week in a row he’s failed to get out on a screen and make a key block. This one was costly, as Brown fumbled this one.
  • To say Washington has problems on the offensive line is a MASSIVE understatement. Josh Conerly and Brandon Coleman both had their issues throughout the game. I already talked about Paul above.
  • Losing our best offensive lineman to an apparent concussion is really going to hurt. Here’s hoping Sam Cosmi doesn’t miss too much time…
  • Houston, we have a kicking problem (yet again). However, I’m going to give rookie Drew Stevens a VERY long leash.
  • OT Andrew Wylie has absolutely NO BUSINESS playing left tackle.
  • WR Dyami Brown got robbed. He also had a fumble, which I’m not 100% pinning on him.
  • CB Rasul Douglas was not as bad as Sainristil, but he did allow six receptions on seven targets for 61 yards.
  • I thought EDGEDorance Armstrong looked pretty good in his return to action. He registered five total tackles (three solo) and two pressures. They moved him around a bit and I thought he played well against the run.
  • OC David Blough and DC Daronte Jones reversed roles this week. Last week, Jones was nearly a stud while Blough was a dud for his play calling. Against Dallas, Jones’ secondary got absolutely TORCHED, while the offense under Blough looked functional. An unfortunate injury, a few missed big plays and calls from the refs that went against the Commanders made the output look worse than it was.
  • C Nick Allegretti wasn’t a complete liability like he was against Philly. Hey, it’s a start…
  • For the second week in a row, Washington’s defense failed to register a turnover.

The Injury

  • First of all, this was an ACCIDENT. Could Dan Quinn have chosen to kick the field goal here? ABSOLUTELY, but let’s get this straight. This was NOT a decision that put his quarterback’s health at risk, so no need to play revisionist history. As mad as I am over this latest injury, we can’t blame Chris Paul either for stepping on his foot, just as we can’t blame David Blough for having him under center.

item.title: Seahawks Droppings: New starting quarterback, same results for streaking ‘Hawks
item.description: Seattle rolls with Drew Lock at QB, setting franchise records along the way.
item.content:encoded:
It doesn’t matter who’s playing for the Seattle Seahawks right now…they’re on a freakin’ roll! Drew Lock stepped right in for Sam Darnold and led the Seahawks to a 31-7 drubbing of the Arizona Cardinals in the desert. This win pushed Seattle’s winning streak to a franchise record 12 games in a row, and was also the 10th consecutive victory over the Cardinals. 

The Seahawks are on an absolute heater right now. Seattle got off to a hot start on the first drive with an 82-yard TD pass from Lock to Jaxon Smith-Njigba. From then on until halftime, it was a bit of a struggle with some drops, fumbles, and a failed 4th down play. Heading into halftime, the score was 7-7 with the Cardinals hanging around and feeling good. Then, the Seahawks threw the Cardinals out the front door like Uncle Will from Fresh Prince of Bel Air. Seattle rallied off 24 straight points including a soul crushing drive that took up most of the fourth quarter. They kept ramming it down Arizona’s throat, and finished it off with a 1-yard AJ Barner “Barn Yard” TD. It was Seattle imposing their will and it was glorious! What a statement. 

Seahawks Droppings

  • Drew Lock played a fantastic game, throwing for 3 TDs and taking care of the ball. His completion percentage would’ve been even better if not for some uncharacteristic drops by JSN and Rashid Shaheed. Lock was poised, escaped pressure, and whistled some truly beautiful throws in there. Sam Darnold will still be the QB when he’s healthy, but the Seahawks have to feel pretty good about their QB situation. 
  • Brian Fleury showed that he runs a QB-friendly system. Remember when Mac Jones looked great playing in the place of an injured Brock Purdy for the San Francisco 49ers? Same system. Fleury called plenty of run plays to soften the Cardinals defense before hitting them with the pass. Then, he used the run game to deliver the knockout blow. Just a beautiful execution of the game plan. 
  • JSN is inevitable. No matter how many people you put on him or how you try to stop him, it seems impossible right now. 9 catches on 11 targets for 155 yards and 3 TDs. Within those catches were some vital third down conversions. JSN can literally do everything at the wide receiver position, a total luxury for Seattle. 
  • Let’s give it up one time for the RBs! Price’s fumble notwithstanding, the RB room showed out. Emmanuel Wilson led way with 92 yards while Price chipped in 52 of his own. The rookie injured his chest, so hopefully that won’t hold him out. Wilson, taking the lion’s share of the carries after Price went out, looked quick, decisive, and powerful. He always fell forward and rarely was tackled by the first defender. When Charbonnet comes back, the Seahawks might now have a three-headed monster in the backfield. 
  • Seattle’s defense absolutely suffocated Arizona’s offense after allowing a TD on 4th down to Trey McBride. They shut down the run, only allowing 70 rushing yards, which was padded by a garbage time explosive run on the last drive. Jacoby Brissett didn’t do much better throwing the ball, managing 81 yards passing with an interception. In the postgame presser, Leonard Williams (who had a fantastic sack by the way), mentioned how they want to play defense like a boa constrictor. Mission accomplished today.
  • I feel like I need to mention Julian Love once again. That was one of the best INTs I’ve ever seen, getting his hands underneath the ball and keeping it off the turf while sliding towards the boundary. Love has always been a good player, but I feel like he’s entering the blue-chip territory.
  • It was good to see both Tory Horton and Nick Emmanwori get some snaps. They’ll be worked in even more in the coming weeks and will both provide explosive potential on each sides of the ball.

The Seahawks made a statement with this victory. No matter what the starting lineup looks like, when they play like Seahawks, they’re going to be tough to beat. Relentlessly physical and opportunistic in all three phases, this 31-7 beatdown is an example of the tidal wave that Seattle can bring on their opponents. What a beautiful representation of the game of football!

item.title: Fan Notes from the Patriots’ win over the Steelers
item.description: Notes, thoughts and musings from the Patriots’ 20-3 win in Week 2.
item.content:encoded:
And just like that, we’re back in the win column.

The Patriots needed to bounce back after a rough season opener, and they were able to take care of business at home against the Steelers. It wasn’t the greatest win in team history, and losing Mike Onwenu really, really sucks. But 20-3 against a 2025 playoff team isn’t anything to laugh at.

  1. Opening the season on a Wednesday night made it feel like nine years had passed between Week 1 and Week 2 for this team. It also feels like an unfathomable amount of activity has transpired between then and now. But honestly, there really hasn’t been that much.
  2. What should be familiar, though — at least to those who have been around for a while — is the narrative surrounding a win like this one. Double digits, kept the opponent out of the end zone, plenty to be happy about, a strong bounceback, incredible defensive performance… and all the Boston media can talk about is what a disaster this team is.
  3. We used to get wins like this all the time during the Brady Era; the Patriots would beat the Ravens or the Bills or the Steelers by 14 or 23 points and Tom Brady would throw for 248 with a TD and a pick and all anyone could hear was how many points the team left on the field and how sluggish the offense looked. I’d be totally fine with New England racking up wins like this one for the rest of the season.
  4. That said… did Drake Maye look great out there? Not at all. That’s four interceptions in two games for him. And this New England offense hasn’t found its second gear yet. No Patriots receiver caught more than three passes all game and other than a few chunk plays, there weren’t a ton of offensive highlights. But that’s just fine with me. This was as close to a must-win game as you can get in Week 2, and the Patriots were in control from start to finish.
  5. Mostly because of the defense, which looked lights-out. If Pittsburgh had an offensive highlight, I certainly missed it. And this isn’t a terrible Steelers team. They aren’t great, but they aren’t trash either.
  6. If history is any indicator, Rhamondre Stevenson will fumble three more times over the next two weeks, and then he won’t have another one for the rest of the year.
  7. I’m trying to be as objective as possible on the heels of this win, as it’s easy to become a prisoner of the moment. It felt like New England had this one well in hand from the opening kickoff, and game-planned accordingly based on that confidence. I’m not overly concerned about Drake Maye, and I’m not sure whether or not I should be. I can’t figure out whether or not Romeo Doubs is any good. I don’t really know what this offense is supposed to look like sans A.J. Brown. I’m very concerned about the offensive line depth now that Onwenu is out with what seems to be a broken ankle. I’m happy with what I saw from the defense and feel like the offense doesn’t need to score 40 points a game if the D can remain consistent. But mostly, I’m just happy with the win.
  8. I apologize for the brevity of today’s Fan Notes; this was my annual game that I attended with my old man, bringing our streak up to 27 years now of going to at least one game per year. My plan was to jot some thoughts down on my phone as I was watching, but the degernates in Section 307 made that very difficult.
  9. I’m also still reeling from the price of beer at Gillette these days. Two aluminum bottles of Bud Light can run you damn near $40 if you’re not careful. If drinking alchohol didn’t have so many scientifically proven health benefits, I’d probably give it up due to lack of affordability.
  10. But I’m glad I got to see Aaron Rodgers play live at least once, even though he’s nowhere close to what he once was. I know he has said that it’s his last season a few times now, but I imagine that this really has to be it.
  11. The things I’m going to be paying attention to this week, besides how they’re going to reshuffle the offensive line:
  12. What will the backfield split look like? Henderson is clearly the big-play threat, but Stevenson is still a more consistent between-the-tackles runner when he actually hangs onto the ball.
  13. I don’t think there’s anything to be worried about in regards to the kicking game. But I also don’t trust how not worried I am about the kicking game.
  14. With two road games coming up against the Jaguars and Bills, I can’t see a duplicate of today’s performance leading to a 2-0 record over that stretch.
  15. I also think that the Patriots could very easily go 2-0 over that stretch. This might not be an overly exciting offense, but they have the pieces in place to win games. I’d love to see Drake Maye go all Chad Pennington on the NFL in 2026 and put together a series of 18-play, 48-yard drives that eat up nine minutes of play clock and end in points. That might be the formula going forward.

I think we’re going to know a lot more about this team by this time next week. The Jags looked like a completely different team yesterday than they did Week 1, and the Pats have a legit chance to build some momentum. I can also 100% see a scenario where they play like complete crap and close out the first quarter of the season at 1-3. But there are a lot of positives to build on here.

item.title: Steelers report card: Bad days for Aaron Rodgers, offensive line vs Patriots
item.description: The Steelers defense graded better but missed on some critical opportunities to keep Pittsburgh's offense in the game for longer.
item.content:encoded:
The Pittsburgh Steelersdropped a 20-3 decision to the New England Patriots in their first road game of the 2026 season on Sunday, Sept. 20 in Foxboro, Mass. 

Despite the lack of scoring, the Steelers weren’t out of it until the fourth quarter, when Elijah Porter returned a fumble by quarterback Aaron Rodgers 19 yards for a touchdown that put New England up by three scores. 

Still, the meek performance offensively is a discouraging early season sign of how much work coach Mike McCarthy’s team has to do to get on the level of the reigning AFC champions. 

Here’s USA TODAY’s report card for each position group. 

Required reading: 5 takeaways from Steelers' Week 2 dud vs. Patriots, including DK Metcalf

Quarterback – C

This was the type of game where a younger Aaron Rodgers might have had a better day in the face of pressure. He was sacked four times and fumbled twice for a pair of strip sacks. It’s easy to blame the offensive line – and we certainly will here shortly. Rodgers’ lack of escapability at this stage of his career was nevertheless noticeable, and he didn’t do anything else Sunday that would distinguish himself from league-average QBs. 

Running backs – C

Jaylen Warren and Rico Dowdle aren’t getting enough run blocking. The amount of contact at or near the line of scrimmage is too great for 100-yard days to be expected from them right now. Last season, however, Warren and team MVP Kenneth Gainwell found ways to be safety valves for Rodgers in games exactly like this one where the pass rush was heavy and the receivers weren’t doing much downfield. Sunday, Warren had two catches for 34 yards, with 26 of those yards coming on a single garbage time catch. Dowdle had two catches for 22 yards. That’s not good enough, even if McCarthy’s passing game isn’t designed to work through the backs to the same extent former OC Arthur Smith’s was. 

Receivers – D

DK Metcalf no-showed again. He’d registered just two catches for two yards before the Steelers fell behind in 20-3 in the fourth quarter. Roman Wilson continues to be an enigma. He had five catches that somehow went for a total of just 28 yards. Germie Bernard had a nice first-half drive, on which he caught four passes for 35 yards. He also bobbled the ball on a fourth-quarter pass, leading to a Patriots interception. And he did not register another grab after that solid early drive. 

Tight ends – B-

Pat Freiermuth had a ho-hum day of four catches for 32 yards. Darnell Washington had one catch for seven yards. The running game wasn’t nearly good enough for him to get credit for his blocking. It adds up to a forgettable effort. 

Offensive line – D

The poor run blocking is the root of this offense’s issues. It makes the Steelers one dimensional and reliant on the pass to accomplish pretty much anything. Fans are upset about the protection of Rodgers as well, and there’s a level on which that’s valid. It’s also true that the volume of pass blocking snaps has spiked through the first two games, which gives opponents more opportunities to get to Rodgers over the course of a game. Some pressure is simply going to leak through even with decent pass blocking. In this way, the issues with the run blocking compound and simply must improve. 

Defensive line – B-

Take away TreVeyon Henderson’s 39-yard touchdown run and a 24-yard gallop from Rhamondre Stevenson later in the game, and the run defense numbers otherwise look pretty good. The Patriots averaged fewer than three yards on their other 26 carries for the afternoon. Alas, permitting those game-changing plays undermines that good work. 

Linebackers – B+ 

T.J. Watt had another nice day with 1.5 sacks. Alex Highsmith added one of his own, and Patrick Queen added an interception of Maye that denied a New England threat. The only glaring downside was a 30-yard pass allowed by Payton Wilson that set up one of the Patriots’ field goal drives. 

Secondary – C

Safety Jaquan Brisker and cornerbacks Jamel Dean and Asante Samuel Jr. were targeted a total of nine times and allowed eight catches that went for 184 of Drake Maye’s 208 yards. Samuel was beaten badly on Romeo Doubs’ 63-yard catch that helped New England push its lead to 10 points with a second-half field goal. Brisker had a pair of missed tackles. This group misses Joey Porter Jr. 

Coaching – C 

McCarthy accepted blame for the performance, telling reporters: "When the detail is not right, that starts with the coaching, and we have to get that cleaned up." That seems like an apt assessment. There weren’t any dramatically bad personnel or play-calling decisions that stand out. The execution was simply poor and has been for two weeks on offense. The work on the practice field needs to yield more. 

This article originally appeared on USA TODAY: Steelers report card: Bad days for Aaron Rodgers, offensive line vs Patriots

item.title: Colts coach Shane Steichen explains decision to settle for a field goal against Patrick Mahomes in overtime
item.description: Patrick Mahomes made another team pay after giving him way too much time to lead a game-winning drive.
item.content:encoded:
During the current Kansas City Chiefs dynasty, one mantra has proved true more than the rest: There's always enough time on the clock for Patrick Mahomes to do something special. Unfortunately for the Indianapolis Colts and their fans, head coach Shane Steichen seemed to forget that rule during the team's overtime loss to the Chiefs on Sunday night.

With the Colts trailing by three — and roughly three minutes left to play — Steichen put his faith in his defense, deciding to kick a game-tying field goal and give the ball back to Mahomes instead of going for it on fourth-and-8 from the Chiefs' 13. You already know what happened next.

The Colts made the kick to tie the game, but then Mahomes drove the Chiefs down the field and got the team in position for a game-winning field goal as time expired. The Chiefs converted that kick, winning 33-30.

After the game, Steichen explained his thinking on that fourth-down play. The coach said he told quarterback Daniel Jones to go for it if the Chiefs' defense gave Jones a good look. But if the defense presented a less-than-optimal look, Jones was told to just take the field goal.

Despite admitting he gave Jones that option, Steichen said the team wanted that to be the final possession of the game, per ESPN.

"We wanted it to be the last possession," Steichen said.

Steichen called timeout, during which he said he told Jones, "If you love it, man, let's go at it. Let's go win this thing. But if it's not the right look ... let's kick the field goal here."

Steichen also defended his play calling prior to that fourth down. On the first play of the drive, Jones found wideout Laquan Treadwell for a 48-yard gain. That set the Colts up with a first down at the 17-yard line. In a situation where the team needed only a touchdown to win the game, Steichen opted to run the ball twice with Jonathan Taylor. The Chiefs were ready for that, causing Taylor to lose three yards.

Steichen said he wasn't trying to be conservative with those play calls, he simply wanted to end the contest with the ball in Taylor's hands. On the surface, it's not the worst strategy, as Taylor is the team's best offensive player and scored two touchdowns earlier in the game.

Knowing that, however, the Chiefs were able to easily counter those play calls, putting the game in the hands of Jones.

That decision paid off. Jones ran on third down after he was unable to find an open man. That set up the crucial fourth-and-8 … and led to the Colts deciding to take the points.

While going for it on fourth-and 8 would have been a risky move, Steichen ultimately decided to trust his defense against Mahomes. That strategy ended the way it has many times before, with Mahomes coming out on top.

If there's an upside for the Colts, it's — hopefully — that Steichen learned his lesson. If his team can rally from an 0-2 start to make the playoffs, Steichen could find himself in a similar spot against the Chiefs in the playoffs.

In that moment, Colts fans will have to hope Steichen won't hesitate. Thanks to Sunday's game, he knows what happens when you give the ball back to Mahomes with a game on the line.

item.title: Report: Saints LT Kelvin Banks believed to have a high-ankle sprain
item.description: The Saints came back to beat the Ravens in Baltimore on Sunday, but it looks like their attempt to build on that win will come without their starting left tackle.
item.content:encoded:
The Saints came back to beat the Ravens in Baltimore on Sunday, but it looks like their attempt to build on that win will come without their starting left tackle.

Kelvin Banks was carted off during the 24-17 win and Ian Rapoport of NFL Media reports that Banks is believed to have a high-ankle sprain. Banks is set to have an MRI to evaluate the extent of the injury.

High-ankle sprains often keep players out for weeks, so a stint on injured reserve could be in the cards for the 2025 first-round pick.

Asim Richards replaced Banks after he hurt his ankle on Sunday and is in line to take over as the starter for any future absences.

item.title: Giants vs. Titans odds: Opening lines for Week 3 matchup
item.description: The NY Giants open as strong favorites at home over the 0-2 Tennessee Titans
item.content:encoded:
The New York Giants haven’t played the Los Angeles Rams yet, but it’s already Week 3 for the 30 other teams.

The Giants still have business to take care of, but they’ll be hosting the Tennessee Titans Sunday at MetLife Stadium at 1 p.m. The Giants open as 6.5-point favorites at home against the 0-2 Titans, per FanDuel, though the line may change based on what happens tonight.

This is one of the games that we’ve had circled since January and it promises to be rich with storylines. The Giants and Titans are inextricably linked after an offseason rife with cross-pollination.

These two teams last met in 2022, with the Giants stunning the Titans who were coming off of a 12-4 season. The Giants came away with a win when the Titans missed a last-second field goal. That game started the Titans’ decline, while the Giants rode the momentum to a 9-7-1 season, a trip to the playoffs, and their first post-season win since 2011.

This time around, the game will feature a gaggle of former Giants making their return to the Meadowlands. Starting slot receiver Wan’Dale Robinson, starting center Austin Schlottman, and second tight end Daniel Bellinger are all featured on the Titans’ offense. Meanwhile, cornerback Cor’Dale Flott is starting for Tennessee’s defense, though he missed last week’s game with a quad injury. His status will be something to monitor.

The Giants attempted to re-sign both Robinson, who was the Giants’ leading receiver a season ago, and Flott, but were outbid by the cap-rich, talent-poor Titans.

This will also feature a different reunion of former teammates. Tennessee drafted Ohio State wide receiver Carnell Tate with the fourth overall pick. The Giants drafted his teammate, LB Arvell Reese with the very next pick.

The highlight of the storylines is the return of Brian Daboll to New York. Daboll was, as we all remember, the Giants’ head coach from 2022 to 2025, when he was fired mid-season. He was hired by Robert Saleh to be Tennessee’s offensive coordinator and develop quarterback Cam Ward. On the flip side, former Titans’ head coachBrian Callahan is now the Giants’ QB coach and passing game coordinator.

Adding to the intrigue, the Titans nearly took down the Philadelphia Eagles in Week 2. The Titans were almost completely bereft of talent a year ago, and they’re going to be a work in progress this year. But perhaps their rebuild is progressing fast than we anticipated — or perhaps the Eagles aren’t as good as many believe.

It feels odd to see the Giants as strong favorites on game day — whether at home or on the road — and this game promises to be far more interesting than the spread may suggest.
